summary: Tekhenu is a dense Tascini/Turczi euro where you rotate a central obelisk to unlock different action spaces and spend dice as workers whose strength grows as you invest in them. Turns are short but every decision ripples across several interlocking subsystems (temple building, gods' favor, monuments), so the game rewards planning several rounds ahead.
praised: variety of viable strategies and paths to points
criticised: overwhelming rulebook and iconography for a first play
thin theme bolted onto abstract systems

interaction.detail: Players compete for limited spaces around the rotating obelisk and can be shut out of an action if someone takes it first, and dice/worker strength is a shared, visible resource others plan around. Most of each player's engine (temple grid, monuments) lives on their own board, so a large share of the state is private.

scoring.how_you_win: You build up the obelisk, place temple offering discs, and complete card objectives across a fixed sequence of epochs punctuated by Maat's reckoning; whoever has the most total points when the last epoch ends wins.
